summary: You present a clear Australian mission rationale and a logical project structure, and Image 1 gives a useful week-by-week plan. To reach the next rubric level, define measurable mission requirements, strengthen the plan with contingencies and specific sources, and show defensible technical results. Correct the proposed 600 km geostationary orbit and reconcile the editing schedule in the text and chart.
next_steps: In Mission Concept & Rationale, turn the broad monitoring aim into measurable objectives: specify coverage, observation frequency, data products, users’ needs and operational constraints. Distinguish ocean acidification from the main cause of mass bleaching (elevated water temperatures), and qualify the reef-wide coral mortality claims with reliable sources and scope.

In Project Plan & Preliminary Progress, name the sources you will use and add contingencies for delays or design changes. Make the editing dates agree with Image 1, and explain how the schedule supports the mission work. Replace the 600 km geostationary proposal with a physically feasible orbit and justify its coverage of the reef.

To strengthen your technical progress, build on your STK tutorials and research by including initial calculations or simulations—for example, orbit coverage or revisit estimates—with a brief interpretation. In the report, give sources full bibliographic details, check that citations are consistent, and refine awkward phrasing.

criteria.C1: Your Mission Concept & Rationale identifies the Australian benefit, likely users and monitoring purpose, with supporting sources. For the next level, define measurable objectives and requirements, including coverage, data products and operational constraints; distinguish acidification from temperature-driven bleaching and qualify mortality claims.
criteria.C2: Your week-by-week plan and Image 1 cover key mission tasks and make completion broadly plausible. For the next level, specify information sources, add contingencies, explain how the schedule serves this mission, and reconcile the editing dates in the prose and chart.
criteria.C3: You have researched the monitoring concept and bleaching and completed STK tutorials 1–4. For the next level, present and interpret useful preliminary calculations or simulations. Resolve the 600 km geostationary claim: that altitude is low Earth orbit; geostationary altitude is about 35,786 km above Earth.
criteria.C4: Your headings provide a logical structure, and Image 1 is a labelled, legible Gantt chart. For the next level, make the schedule consistent throughout, replace bare URLs with complete reference details, and polish awkward phrasing so the report reads professionally.
